pages.text: PHP: What is it and why did it spark a global cyber security scramble? Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live What is PHP and why did it spark a global cyber-security scramble? 23 October 2026 Share Save Add as preferred on Google Liv McMahon , Technology reporter and Osmond Chia , Business reporter How did AI discover the internet's massive cyber-security risk? For more than a decade, serious flaws had gone undetected in the technology underpinning much of the internet. It took AI to bring them to light and caused a global cyber-security alert. Researchers who helped surface the vulnerabilities in PHP - a popular server-side programming language used in web development for decades - warned platforms which use it could be exposed to potential hacks. Governments and cyber-security agencies rushed to contain the fallout , urging website owners to check if their sites were affected and, if so, install updates to patch the issue or consider going offline. There have been no reports of any successful exploits of the flaw, coined php2shell, so far. But in the days since the issues came to light, disruption to sites and services has continued to ripple around the world. What is PHP? Most people may not have heard of PHP, but they probably interact with it daily. It stands for PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor, an open-source, back-end programming language which runs on a web server. Nestled in a cirque and fed by snowmelt and springs, these lakes are not only visually stunning but also possess an excellent trout fishery. The lakes are surrounded by a rare remnant population of white bark and limber pines; stands of quaking aspen and mountain mahogany are also found throughout the area. Fall brings a riot of color found in few other places in northern Nevada. The spectacular scenery and vistas, combined with outstanding recreational opportunities, draw thousands of visitors annually. Despite being one of the most highly visited recreational areas in the region, the area still appears pristine. Day hiking, horseback riding, rock climbing, hunting, fishing, and camping are all popular in the area. Visitors enjoy a true primitive recreation experience, without trails or facilities. Located approximately 100 miles (161 km) northeast of Fairbanks, this 27-mile (44 km) hiking trail traverses a series of alpine ridge tops entirely above timberline. The trail was built for hikers, but is open to all forms of non-motorized use. The Pinnell Mountain Trail is marked with rock cairns as it crosses open tundra with views north to the Yukon River and south to the Alaska Range. Wooden posts along the trail show the mileage from the start at Eagle Summit to the trail's end at Twelvemile Summit. Two shelters provide refuge from storms, but hikers should come prepared for unpredictable, dramatic alpine weather. Nearly 50 volunteers, partners and riders spent National Public Lands Day turning trail talk into teamwork and community pride into on‑the‑ground stewardship. pages.text: Plain Writing Plain Writing Skip Navigation Within About the U.S. Census Bureau Plain Writing The Plain Writing Act of 2010 requires federal agencies to communicate clearly in a way the public can understand. The Act states that plain writing means "writing that is clear, concise, well-organized, and follows other best practices appropriate to the subject or field and intended audience." The Census Bureau has long sought to improve communications with the public, dependent as we are on public cooperation in our censuses and surveys. We at the Census Bureau are committed to writing new documents in plain language. The Plain Writing Act requires federal agencies to use plain language in public documents, particularly those that — Explain a benefit or service. Show how to apply for a benefit or service. Meet a federal requirement. The Census Bureau follows all reguirements and guidance provided by our parent agency the U.S. Department of Commerce. The National Monument includes the A.G. Gaston Motel, which served as the headquarters for the Birmingham campaign. Here they strategized and made critical decisions about the non-violent campaign that targeted Birmingham’s segregation laws and practices. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Canyons of the Ancients National Monument | Colorado View Map In Full Screen Canyons of the Ancients National Monument, located in the Four Corners region of southwestern Colorado, protects a stunning cultural landscape with the highest known density of archaeological sites in the United States. Encompassing 176,000 acres of public lands, the Monument features more than 8,300 documented sites—including villages, kivas, field houses, cliff dwellings, petroglyphs, and ancient roadways—with estimates suggesting over 30,000 yet to be recorded. These sites offer a window into over 12,000 years of human history, primarily shaped by Ancestral Puebloan cultures and their descendants. The area continues to be a living landscape used today for traditional purposes, recreation, hunting, livestock grazing, and energy development. It also encompasses Cross Canyon , Sego Lily, and Cahone Canyon Wilderness Study Areas. While exploring the Monument’s canyons, mesas, and desert terrain, visitors are reminded to Visit with Respect and Leave No Trace to protect the resources that define this unique place. But in 2001, a thriving population was found on land south of Santiago Photograph By SELECTPHOTO/ALAMY STOCK PHOTO ENVIRONMENT VANISHING Plant extinctions are shaking Earth’s green foundation Compared with birds, mammals, and amphibians, more plants have vanished in the wild since 1900. What’s the cost to ecosystems? By Michael Greshko 3 min read This story appears in the October 2019 issue of National Geographic magazine. When you conjure up “extinction” in your mind’s eye, you probably see an animal—a dodo , perhaps, or a Tasmanian tiger . But the biodiversity crisis isn’t just faunal, it’s floral too. Since the 1750s, at least 571 species of plants have gone extinct in the wild, according to a global survey recently published in Nature Ecology & Evolution . More than eight plant species have disappeared every three years, on average, since 1900. pages.text: Polar Bears in the Roman Colosseum? | National Geographic By Candida Moss Published September 28, 2026 Want to make sure you get every Stones & Bones newsletter? Put your email here . There’s a strange and intriguing reference in the writings of a first-century Roman poet who describes a showdown between bears and seals (or, as he called them, “sea-calves”) in the Colosseum. Only polar bears are known to fight seals, so this raises a question no modern scholar has yet been able to answer: How on Earth would arctic bears have traveled to the heart of the Roman Empire? A clue to the ursine mystery has recently emerged—in the first English language book on Scandinavian Roman-era history, Dagfinn Skre's The Northern Routes to Kingshi p . Skre places Sweden, Norway, and Denmark at the periphery of the empire, showing that Denmark was only a four-week march from the Roman frontier. And in fact, the Roman military was recruiting from the region by the late first century A.D. So the social networks and infrastructure were in place to facilitate the movement of exotic animals that Rome craved for its spectacles. I reached out to Michael Kulikowski, a professor of classics at Penn State who wrote about Skre’s work for the London Review of Books , for more on how polar bears could have ended up on the sands of Rome’s most famous arena. pages.description: It was one of history’s most dramatic moments—but the eruption of Mount Vesuvius wasn’t a single disaster. Recent evidence reveals how three settlements faced three distinct fates, reshaping our understanding of how ancient Romans lived and died.
pages.text: Pompeii's Secrets: How AI is Rewriting the Story of Mount Vesuvius | National Geographic By Sam Kean Photographs by Paolo Verzone Video by Massimo Nicolaci Published July 23, 2026 Outside, the world was vanishing. A scum of ash was thickening on the surface of the Gulf of Naples, and black fumes were swallowing the sky above. In a waterfront warehouse in the Roman town of Oplontis, five dozen people cowered in terror. Some clutched gold coins and jewelry—family wealth snatched up in panic. Others gripped common iron tools and little more. One young woman hugged her swollen belly, terrified for the unborn child inside. Their ages and social classes varied widely, but they’d likely all gathered in a storeroom on the water’s edge for the same reason: to await a rescue boat they were increasingly fearful would never come. In A.D. 79, Mount Vesuvius blew its top, raining ash over the Campania region of Italy, near modern-day Naples, and burying surrounding communities beneath as much as 60 feet of volcanic debris. What happened that day in A.D. 79 began with a single event, the eruption of Mount Vesuvius . But each settlement in the volcano’s shadow—including the most famous, Pompeii —experienced a distinct catastrophe depending on its location relative to the volcano and the timing, speed, and direction of the material Vesuvius spewed. A handful of lucky folks within those communities escaped. Pregnancy and Rubella July 11, 2025 Español Key points Rubella is very dangerous for developing babies and can cause congenital rubella syndrome (CRS). Anyone who is not vaccinated against rubella is at risk of getting the disease. You should make sure you are vaccinated against rubella before you get pregnant. Risk factors Rubella is very dangerous during pregnancy If you are planning to get pregnant, you should make sure you are protected against rubella beforehand. Anyone who is not vaccinated against rubella is at risk of getting the disease. If you get rubella during pregnancy, you are at risk for miscarriage or stillbirth. Your developing baby is at risk for severe birth defects with devastating, lifelong consequences. Infection with rubella virus causes the most severe damage during early in pregnancy, especially in the first 12 weeks (first trimester). MMR vaccine protects against rubella Although rubella was declared eliminated from the United States in 2004, cases can occur when unvaccinated people are exposed to infected people. Sin embargo, si usted presentó una declaración de casado en conjunto, no puede iniciar un rastreo utilizando los sistemas automatizados. Debe llamar y hablar con un representante para iniciar el proceso o descargue y complete un Formulario 3911, Declaración del Contribuyente sobre el Reembolso PDF . Su reclamo por un reembolso perdido se procesa en una de dos maneras: Si el cheque no fue cobrado, recibirá un reembolso de reemplazo una vez que se cancele el cheque original. That means thinking through your budget, determining how much you need to earn, and considering whether work might have an impact on any public benefits you currently receive. On this page, you will find answers to important questions and additional resources to help you get ready for your new job. Frequently Asked Questions How can I prepare financially for a job? pages.text: Preparing for Retirement | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Preparing for Retirement Financial security in retirement doesn't just happen. It takes planning and commitment and money. Your employer's retirement savings plan is an essential part of your future financial security. It is important to understand how your plan works and what benefits you will receive. Learn about the rights and responsibilities you have under the federal law that governs your plan, the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA). Remember to review your financial plans at least once a year to see if you need to make changes to stay on track for a secure retirement. Don't touch your retirement savings. The longer you leave the money there, the more time it has to grow. When you are thinking about retiring, be sure you understand the documents governing your health care plan. Although some employers continue to provide health care benefits to their retired employees, private-sector employers are not required to provide retiree health benefits. If you want to retire early, consider what you will do for health coverage before you are eligible for Medicare. Esta página tiene recursos para ayudarlo a responder sus preguntas sobre las vacunas contra la influenza (gripe). Medidas y estrategias de prevención Tómese el tiempo para ponerse una vacuna contra la influenza. Prevención y control de la neumonía Para todos 23 de jul. del 2026 English (US) Puntos clave La neumonía es una infección de los pulmones. La neumonía afecta a millones de personas en todo el mundo cada año. La neumonía a menudo se puede prevenir y, generalmente, se puede tratar. Puede reducir su riesgo de contraer neumonía con vacunas y otras prácticas de vida saludables Información general La vacunación y el tratamiento adecuado (como antibióticos y antivirales) podrían prevenir muchas muertes cada año a causa de la neumonía. La neumonía afecta a muchos adultos en los Estados Unidos La mayoría de las personas afectadas por la neumonía en los Estados Unidos son adultas . Los datos de los CDC muestran que más de 41 000 personas murieron de neumonía en los Estados Unidos en el 2022. ¿Quiénes están en riesgo? Algunas personas están en mayor riesgo de contraer neumonía debido a la edad , otras condiciones médicas y ciertos comportamientos .
